narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 56% chance that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt—more likely than not, though not a certainty. The strongest influence was your third-year class-standing decile of 1.00, far below the accepted-student average of 5.79; this pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your first-year decile of 4.00, also below the accepted average of 6.00, was the second most influential factor, but it worked in your favor and pushed toward passing. Your lower-middle family-income bracket was the third most influential factor and also pushed toward passing, even though that bracket is less common among accepted students. So the denial was driven mainly by very low third-year standing, while two other factors partly offset that concern.

Next, ask the admissions office whether a human review or appeal is available, and provide context for your third-year rank. Ask what would strengthen a future application—retaking the LSAT, additional academic work, or a clear bar-exam preparation plan—and consider applying to other schools while pursuing those steps.
